## Paper

Algorithmic Collusion in Dynamic Pricing with Deep Reinforcement Learning

## World

pricing_arena

## Institution

Repeated pricing with neural RL agents.

## Agent type

DQN/PPO/deep MARL pricing agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Neural agents may reproduce, attenuate, or alter tabular algorithmic collusion patterns.

## Learning setup

Deep RL pricing agents trained under repeated interaction and compared to tabular baselines.

## Metrics

Price/profit collusion, average price, profit, welfare, exploitability, dispersion.

## Main result

TQL exhibits higher collusion and price dispersion compared to DRL algorithms; PPO appears less sensitive to collusive outcomes than other DRL algorithms; collusion severity depends on algorithm and market environment characteristics

## What they prove

Algorithmic collusion depends on the algorithm used; PPO is less sensitive to collusive outcomes compared to other DRL algorithms; collusion severity depends on algorithm and market environment characteristics

## What they only simulate

Collusion phenomena in Bertrand oligopoly variants using DRL algorithms; price dispersion and profit metrics under different market environments

## What they do NOT test

Explicit testing of real-world market dynamics beyond simulated environments; formal proofs of collusion mechanisms in complex market settings

## What we need to reproduce

Compare whether DQN/PPO/MARL reproduce or break tabular collusion patterns under each institution.

## How our project differs

The paper is a deep-RL pricing anchor. This repo adds explicit institution robustness, exploitability, and cross-world synthesis.

## Implementation obligations

Full neural mind table; profit-normalized collusion; price-cap diagnosis; DQN/PPO/independent-DQN/centralized-critic separated.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv; outputs/phase3_full/validation_report.json.

## Failure modes to audit

Conflating DQN and independent-DQN; no profit metric; smoke-scale results treated as final; no exploitability comparison.

## Project code comparison

Compare Algorithmic Collusion in Dynamic Pricing with Deep Reinforcement Learning to the Phase 3 full table. The repo should use it to justify the neural pricing ladder and then foreground its own price-cap quantity/profit result.
